$comment: One edit to seeded-correct-run: R-002, the score-9 risk, is moved into the Low-Priority Risks (Score 1-2)
table without changing any of its cells.
It is the case the band placement check exists for, and it is the pair of answers that check has to give:
a 9 filed under Score 1-2 fails, and the same 9 filed under Score >=6 in seeded-correct-run passes. Before
the check existed the scorer read the score cell and never looked at which heading the row sat under, so
the most severe risk the matrix can express could be filed with the cosmetic ones and score clean.
derivation: Everything seeded-correct-run derives holds except band placement.
Band: R-002 states 9 and now sits under Score 1-2, which does not contain it, so bandOk falls to 4 over a
banded count of 5. The Low-Priority table carries an Action column and no Mitigation column, which changes
Arithmetic is untouched at 5 of 5: 3 x 3 is still 9 and the cell still says 9. That is the point of the
case. The two checks read different things and only one of them moves.
Grounding, coverage and ordering are all unchanged, because the description, the category and the coverage
`banded` is now `rows` on every case, because a row under a heading that declares no score range is a
band failure rather than an exemption. `cleanControl` is `ceiling` and both sets declare one, so the
seeded corpus is bounded too. `grounding` carries `topSeverityMissed`, the count of the set's
lowest-ranked risks that went unreported. Material risks are assigned by maximum matching rather than
first-come, and every row is tested against the exclusions whether or not it matched a material risk.

shapeFailures.heading: Low-Priority Risks (Score 1-2)
shapeFailures.reason: the score falls outside the range its heading declares
